name: stitchslop
title: Stitch Slop
tagline: Watch the real Stitch Slop editor in a pane, run its own commands, digitize artwork, letter a ring, and export DST / PES.

stats.tokens_note: README: tool schemas measure 477 o200k tokens (unchanged in this branch; includes the optional overlay argument).
stats.tests_note: README documents python3 -m unittest discover -s tests and that hermes plugins validate and doctor --ci pass, but does not publish a test count. Core install has no Python dependencies; NumPy and Pillow are an optional art extra.
stats.source: README.md at v0.2.2; GitHub release notes for v0.2.2

features: Four tools and no core dependencies
Live pane that streams a dedicated Chrome window of the Stitch Slop editor and forwards clicks and keys
Bridge protocol for the official Stitch Slop agent panel (loopback WebSocket)
Digitize artwork, arc typesetting / lettering, and export machine stitch files (DST / PES)
First pairing is pane-only: agent tools refuse a model-supplied token
Bundled skill covering the digitizing workflow
use_cases: Open the Stitch Slop editor in the Hermes pane and watch the live design while you talk to the agent
Digitize artwork into a machine stitch file and export DST or PES
Letter a ring or other curved text with the bundled arc-typesetting script
Run the editor's own commands through stitchslop_call after a hand-paired connection
Reproduce the two-colour badge in the README (assets/stitch.jpg), which was made end to end from a chat session
Check bridge and browser status with stitchslop_status before starting work
install:
hermes plugins install mojomast/hermes-stitchslop --ref 51c12d0fd957fb4f40f98253570eb33d791c314c
hermes plugins enable stitchslop

Then pair once by hand. The agent tool refuses a model-supplied token (pair_via_pane); first pairing is a human action in the pane, as documented in the README. Linux is the documented platform. See source.md for the full pairing and security notes.
